questions.answer: I'd like to think so, yes. I genuinely dislike keeping people waiting, so I usually aim to arrive a little early. To me, being on time is a simple way of showing [[consideration]] for others.

questions.q: How do you feel when other people are late?
questions.answer: It depends on the situation. If it's a friend and only a few minutes, I don't mind at all. But if someone is repeatedly late for professional meetings, I find it quite [[exasperating]], because it wastes everyone's time.

questions.q: Are you good at managing your time?
questions.answer: Mostly, yes. I rely a lot on a simple to-do list, which keeps me on track. I'm not perfect, and things occasionally slip, but planning ahead stops me feeling [[overwhelmed]].

questions.q: Do you usually wear a watch?
questions.answer: Not anymore. I used to wear one my father gave me, but now I just check the time on my phone. I still keep that watch safely in a drawer, though, because it has real [[sentimental value]].

questions.q: Do you think people are busier today than in the past?
questions.answer: I'd say so. With smartphones, we're always reachable, so work often spills into our personal time. Our parents seemed to have clearer boundaries, whereas now life feels far more [[fast-paced]] and demanding.
